subject: Payment path & procurement readiness — next steps for FinTechCorp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Payment path & procurement readiness — next steps for FinTechCorp

Hi Priya / Carl,

Great to meet you both on the call this morning — thanks for walking through the platform use case and expected load. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can align on procurement: 

Summary of key points
- POC scope: 1M tokens over 30 days, targeting a single environment (staging) with a small set of evaluation prompts.
- Expected spend for POC: estimated $2.5k–$4k depending on token usage and batching.
- Production expectations: multi-region, reserved capacity; likely to move to PO-based billing for >$10k/month.

Procurement & payment options (asks for AP)
- Card: FinTechCorp mentioned card is preferred for small POCs (<$5k); we can accept card payments for initial engagement.
- PO / vendor onboarding: For production and committed Dedicated capacity we accept PO. We require a standard vendor onboarding packet (W-9, insurance cert, SOC2 summary).
- Marketplace: You asked whether we are available via cloud marketplace to simplify procurement — we are listed on AWS Marketplace (listing can simplify PO flow for some customers).

Attachments: I attached a short Mutual Action Plan that maps milestones to payment steps and our standard SOW template.

Next steps / asks
1) Priya: Can you confirm whether AP will accept a card for the POC amount, or if a PO is required even for evaluation? If PO, please share the vendor onboarding packet and timeline for approval.
2) Carl: Any constraints from your side on start date? You mentioned wanting to get POC going by mid-March.
3) Connor / Jasmine: I copied you to confirm technical onboarding items and to provide the vendor checklist.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-minute handoff with AP if that helps move the paperwork.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RDF_MutualActionPlan_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carl Evans <carl.evans@fintechcorp.com>, AP Team <ap@fintechcorp.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Payment path & procurement readiness — next steps for FinTechCorp

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. Two quick notes from procurement/AP perspective: 

1) Payment method constraints
- Our AP policy: purchases under $5,000 are typically allowed on corporate card; anything over $5,000 generally requires a PO and vendor onboarding. For ongoing subscriptions or recurring billing (monthly > $10k) AP will insist on PO and Net30 terms.
- For POCs < $5k we can usually do card, but must pre-approve charges with AP.

2) Vendor onboarding items
- We need a completed Vendor Onboarding Form (I attached our standard PDF), W-9, current COI (insurance), and a brief security summary (SOC 2 or equivalent). Please confirm you can provide SOC 2 Type II summary and a point of contact for security review.

3) Marketplace
- AWS Marketplace would be ideal for us — it reduces manual vendor setup. Does Redwood have a listing and support for private offers / invoicing through the marketplace? If yes, please provide the listing link so AP can evaluate.

Timeline
- AP can review a vendor packet in ~7–10 business days after we receive the materials. If we can run the POC on card, that’s the fastest route to start. Ideally we’d decide by 2026-03-15 to keep alignment with our roadmap.

Attached: Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf

Regards,

Priya Shah
Senior Procurement Manager | FinTechCorp
priya.shah@fintechcorp.com

Attachment: Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechcorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Payment path & procurement readiness — next steps for FinTechCorp

Priya — thanks for the details. Quick clarifications from engineering / commercial ops side: 

- Card vs PO: We can absolutely accept a corporate card for the POC (your described $2.5k–$4k range). If you prefer to convert to a PO later for production, we will provide a single consolidated invoice and work with your AP for Net30 terms.

- Vendor onboarding: Happy to supply everything you listed — SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted) and W-9 are attached here, plus our standard SOW template in case you want to scope the pilot formally. Security contact for deeper questions: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>.

- Marketplace: We are listed on AWS Marketplace and support private offers; using marketplace can speed purchasing for some customers but depends on internal AP policies around private offers vs direct vendor setup. Link to our AWS listing: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodXXXXXXXX

Estimated invoicing cadence
- POC (card): one-time charge at start or monthly depending on usage — we can issue a single invoice for the POC period if AP prefers.
- Production (PO): monthly invoicing with Net30 is standard; annual invoicing by agreement is also possible.

Attachments: W-9_Redwood.pdf (W-9), SOW_template.pdf (docx/pdf)

If useful, I can join an introduction call with AP next week to answer any billing or technical questions.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai

Attachments: W-9_Redwood.pdf, SOW_template.pdf

From: Carl Evans <carl.evans@fintechcorp.com>

Cc: AP Team <ap@fintechcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Payment path & procurement readiness — next steps for FinTechCorp

Thanks — that all sounds reasonable. A couple quick items from engineering leadership: 

- Timeline: We still want to start the POC by mid-March. If AP can approve a card payment for the POC we can kick off immediately.
- Production billing: AP will require a PO and NET30 for anything that becomes ongoing/non-trivial.
- Onboarding fee: Do you charge a one-time onboarding/configuration fee for Dedicated capacity or is that scoped into an SOW? Please confirm ballpark so we can budget.

I'll coordinate with Priya and AP, but please send the onboarding cost estimate and SOC 2 summary to expedite our internal review.

Thanks — Carl

Carl Evans
Director of Engineering | FinTechCorp
carl.evans@fintechcorp.com
